transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because things with my husband’s sister have gotten hard. I don’t want to sound like I’m causing trouble or anything, but she’s been working this family business in a way that feels like she’s trying to get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep telling me to let it go or smooth it over, but I’ve been seeing it for more than a year now, and I just… I know what I’m seeing.
Do you believe your husband’s sister is deliberately trying to harm you?

I don’t know if I’d say “harm” exactly… I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. But yes, I do feel like she’s doing it on purpose, with the business and the money. Like she’s trying to get control and leave me out of decisions. People keep telling me it’s just family stuff, but I’ve been watching it for over a year, and I know what I’m seeing.
If your husband or someone else shows you evidence that your sister-in-law is not trying to push you out, are you able to accept that?

I mean… I try to listen when my husband says I’m reading too much into it. I don’t want to be stubborn or cause problems. But honestly, even when people try to explain it away or smooth it over, it doesn’t really change what I’ve been seeing. It’s been going on more than a year with the business and the money, and it still feels like she’s trying to get control and keep me out of decisions.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t noticed anything like voices when nobody’s there. I know how that might sound to ask, but no, that’s not really what’s been happening.
Do you often feel that other people, besides your husband’s sister, are trying to take advantage of you or work against you?

Not really other people, no… I don’t want to sound like I think everybody’s against me. It’s mainly his sister. That’s why I came in, because with the family business and the money, it feels like she’s been working things so she can get control and push me out of decisions. And I know people try to smooth it over, but I’ve been seeing it for more than a year now.
Has anyone shown you clear proof that your husband’s sister is not trying to push you out?

Well… they’ve tried to tell me I’m misunderstanding it, and my husband especially tries to smooth it over. I don’t want to make trouble or be unfair to anyone. But clear proof? No, not really. Nothing that changes what I’ve been seeing.

I came because it really feels like his sister has been working the family business so she can get control of the money and keep me out of decisions. It’s been more than a year, so… I know how it sounds, but I can’t just ignore it.
Has your husband’s sister actually done anything specific that makes you think she is trying to push you out?

Well… yes, I mean, not like one big thing I can hand you on paper, if that’s what you mean. It’s more the way she’s been handling things with the family business… money decisions, conversations happening without me, making it seem like I don’t need to be included.

I don’t want to sound dramatic, doctor. I know families can misunderstand each other. But this has been going on for more than a year, and no matter how people try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing. It feels like she’s trying to get control and push me out.
If you were shown definite proof that your husband’s sister was not trying to push you out, would you believe it?

I’d like to think I would, doctor. I don’t want to be stubborn or make something out of nothing.

But… if I’m being honest, it would have to be very definite, because I’ve been seeing this for more than a year now. The way she handles the family business, the money, keeping me out of decisions… no matter how people try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing. So I’d try to listen, but I don’t know that it would just erase it for me.
If you were shown bank records proving your husband’s sister was not taking control of the money, would you believe them?

I would try to, doctor. I mean, if they were real bank records, I wouldn’t want to argue just to argue.

But I guess… I’d still wonder if that showed everything. Because what I’ve been worried about isn’t only one withdrawal or something like that. It’s how she’s been working the family business, getting control of things, and keeping me out of decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over, and I know I should be fair, but I’ve been seeing this for more than a year now. So I’d look at them, yes… I just don’t know if that would completely settle it for me.
Has this situation with your husband’s sister caused serious problems in your marriage or daily life?

No, I wouldn’t say it’s caused serious problems, not in the way you might mean. My husband and I still manage, and I still do my regular things — my quilting group, choir practice, my GED lessons, and the senior walks.

It’s more that I’m careful now. I don’t trust his sister like I used to, and there are some family gatherings I just don’t feel comfortable going to. But I don’t want to make it sound like my whole life has stopped or anything.
Do you think it is possible that you might be mistaken about your husband’s sister trying to push you out?

I suppose anything is possible, doctor… I don’t want to sound like I think I know better than everybody.

But from where I’m sitting, I don’t think I’m mistaken. I came here because of what I’ve been seeing with my husband’s sister — the way she’s been handling the family business, getting closer to the money side of things, and leaving me out of decisions. People try to make it sound harmless, and I understand they may mean well, but this has been going on for over a year. So… I can say I’d try to consider it, but I still feel I know what I’ve been seeing.
Besides your concerns about your husband’s sister, have you had any other experiences that felt unusual or hard for other people to believe?

No… I don’t think so, doctor. Not really.

I mean, I worry about this situation with his sister, but I haven’t had other strange things happening, if that’s what you mean. Nothing I’d want to make a big deal out of. I try to keep my feet on the ground. Is that the kind of thing you were asking?
Before this situation with your husband’s sister, have you generally been a very suspicious person in other relationships over the years?

I don’t think so… at least, I wouldn’t describe myself that way.

I’ve always tried to get along with people, maybe I’m a little cautious sometimes, but not suspicious like this. I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve been looking for trouble with everyone over the years. This situation just feels different to me. Is that answering what you mean?
Have you done anything to investigate your husband’s sister or protect yourself because of these concerns?

Well… I wouldn’t say I’ve done anything extreme, doctor. I’m not following her around or anything like that.

I have, um… skipped a few family get-togethers, just because I didn’t want to be in a position where things could get twisted or reported back to her. And I’ve been more private about certain plans or money matters. I keep some things to myself now, just to be safe.

But I’m still doing my normal things, you know — taking care of the house, going to church, keeping my routines. I don’t want you to think I’ve let it take over everything. Does that make sense?
Has anyone directly shown you that a decision you thought your husband’s sister made behind your back actually happened for an innocent reason?

Well… people have tried to explain things away, yes. They’ll say, “Oh, she didn’t mean it like that,” or “It was just a misunderstanding,” things like that.

But I can’t honestly say anyone has shown me something that really proves it was innocent. I came here because it’s been over a year of seeing how she works around the family business and the money, and how I get pushed out of decisions. I know that may sound like I’m being difficult, and I don’t want to be, doctor… but no matter how they try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing.
